text: I think I will be able to change universities!!! I still have to send some documents, but they accepted me. I won't know until August if I am really in. I am excited and a little nervous about it.
Just finished Part 5, Volume 11 of Ascendance of a Bookworm. Might start Volume 12 tonight.

Well, after a few intense weeks of weighing my options, I’ve decided to study at TecNM Virtual. These were my options: studying Web Systems Development at UDG, or Computer Systems Engineering at UVEG, UVM, etc. I really like the curriculum at TecNM; it covers the very things I want to study on my own. I don't feel comfortable studying the DOM, for example, without knowing graph theory; which is why I'm leaving UDG; nor do I feel comfortable studying cybersecurity without knowing networking. Studying at UVEG could be a good option too, I’d finish sooner, but I don't know; I just preferred TecNM's curriculum. I'll be taking linear algebra next semester, which is exactly the pace I want. However, it's a very new university, and I'm afraid of ending up being the only student in my cohort, or that I might spend four years on my degree only for something to happen that prevents me from getting my diploma. I don't know... my goal is to pursue a master's degree later on, so I'm pinning all my hopes on TecNM; I'm not turning back. So, I'm counting on you! If any TecNM Virtual administrator sees this, I want you to know that you have a student here who believes in you. Don't let me down, and I won't let you down, pleaseeeeee!!! (；人 ；)

Today I was studying discrete math. I don't know, I was studying discrete math on my own last year. What am I doing? Should I study everything in two years and forget about this? A few years ago, when I was in high school, I asked a teacher about computers. The response was pretty flat, and 3 years later, AI happened boom! I wonder what happened to that person. It's like people here have no vision and their only goal is to make money at any cost. I'm not judging, but what about passion?. My country hasn't developed as much technology, and I feel trapped here, in this system, in this culture. I've asked in several places, and the answer I get is, 'It's not worth it, study everything in two years and move on with your life.' I don't know what to think. I'd like to study web development, I'd like to study operating systems. I've already applied to a few universities, because it's relatively easy to get accepted here, and when I see the classes, see the materials, it's soul-crushing. I wish I could study at an American university, or at least be able to take out a loan to do so, but there are no options, I have no options. And instead of developing things, I'm trapped in this system. I'll study for four and a half years at this university, get my degree, and move on with my life... It's just that I'm on my own. I could just pass the courses without learning anything. How much should I study? How much is enough? I can't keep going down rabbit holes. If I study something, I like to do it thoroughly, but then there are so many things. Who's going to guide me? The university doesn't do that... I don't know... I genuinely envy people in other countries with more options. English courses offer better resources than all the universities I've been to; it's soul-crushing.
